data.name: Sachindra
data.gender_notes: Sachindra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit words 'Sat' (truth) and 'Indra' (Lord of Consciousness). The name Sachindra carries the meaning “Lord of Consciousness” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sachindra usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of consciousness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine truth and pure consciousness.
data.etymology: Sachindra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Consciousness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sachindra total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sachindra holds a rich cultural heritage in Hinduism. It is believed that the name symbolizes the embodiment of truth and wisdom, qualities highly respected and sought after in Hindu society. This name can be equated to having a strong sense of ethical conduct, being honest, and upholding principles essential for personal growth and societal harmony.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Sachindra is a powerful name that resonates with the consciousness of the Divine Lord Indra, who is known to bestow blessings of knowledge, inner wisdom, and insight to those who seek his guidance. By bearing this name, one is thought to be connected to the divine source of consciousness and truth, inspiring a continuous journey of self-discovery and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sachindra: Radiating Truth and Wisdom. A beacon of pure consciousness, enlightening the path to self-realization.

vedic_reference.note: Indra is the king of the Devas, and Sachindra is one who embodies truth and consciousness.

historical_references.reference: Sachindra Rao - A 14th-century Hindu king of the Vijayanagara Empire in South India. He is known for his military conquests and his patronage of the arts, particularly temple building.

Sachin Deva - A Hindu king of the Sisodia Rajput dynasty, ruling from the fort of Chittorgarh in present-day Rajasthan, India. He is known for his valor in battle and his role in the epic poem 'Mahabharata' as a central character.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Sachindra' is of Hindu origin, derived from the Sanskrit word 'Sachindra', which translates to 'God of Truth'. This name has seen modern usage in various contexts, particularly in the realms of Mythology and Spirituality. In social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter, you may find profiles or pages dedicated to 'Sachindra' where people share stories, images, and quotes related to the Hindu deity. Some individuals may also choose to use the name 'Sachindra' as a personal name, reflecting their connection to the divine and their personal values of truth and integrity.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Arjun Sachindra in Delhi, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Sachindra, which means "Lord of Consciousness". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
